items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: after Mercer explained to me that he wanted a perfect triad...

ctx.x: And he explained that Duke wrote everything in triads, which was interesting. Because when I copied the records, I could follow each part. And I would hear the three trumpets

going C, A, E down. But above the third trumpet would be the trombone playing in G. And I couldn't figure out why he was doing that. And after Mercer explained to me that he wanted a perfect triad of an A-minor in the trumpets and a G-minor in the trombones, that's how the G got over the third trumpet. And that clarified a lot of copying arrangements later, when I couldn't be sure what I was hearing. If I followed that principle, it would come out right. Because Duke had told -- he said that he wanted every…

So the first record I copied was "Blue Ramble." And it must have taken me six months to copy that thing and I couldn't get anybody to play it anyhow. You know, the kids in high school sort of -- they weren't that interested in playing.
